Set A gives the window band three bays of paired tall casements between brick piers, a brick back wall with raked horizontal joints and flush vertical joints, a continuous light cast-stone sill course, plinth and cap under an oak head band, plus a copper-lined sill planter, whereas Set B is a plain single window with painted MDF towers and no brick or capping bands.

Set A wraps the room in 0.84 m fixed lights and terrace doors between piers on three walls, runs a bare tawny brick hearth wall with raked horizontal joints and caps every datum (head band, soffit fascia, 0.90 m sill course, hearth plinths, sideboard) with pale cast stone, while Set B uses two wide windows, painted plaster, limestone and a dropped canopy with none of the brick-and-band language.
